story.head: Faulk reaches 500 points as the Red Wings beat the Senators
paras: Carter Mazur picked up his first NHL point. Tim Stützle opened the scoring for the Senators early in the first, but Alex DeBrincat tied it up for Detroit 32 seconds later. Dylan Larkin put the Red Wings ahead for good midway through the period, in his first game of the season. Viktor Arvidsson and Justin Faulk scored two and a half minutes apart early in the second to make it 4-1. Drake Batherson cut Detroit’s lead to 4-2 on the power play less than two minutes later. William Eklund scored his first goal for Ottawa midway through the third to pull the Senators within one. DeBrincat struck again into the empty net with just under a minute left, with Faulk picking up his 500th NHL point on the goal. William Wallinder played his first NHL game and picked up a point. The Sens’ Ridly Greig played his first game of the season, after missing the first two, and picked up an assist. Two players had three-point nights: Lucas Raymond with three assists, and DeBrincat with two goals and an assist.
The Red Wings had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Senators 36-25. John Gibson made 22 saves for the Red Wings, and Samuel Ersson stopped 31 of 35 at the other end.

A scrum at the end of the second sent five players to the box. Greig took three penalties on his own. The Red Wings moved to 1-2-0 and climbed out of last place in the NHL, while the Senators fell to 2-1-0, slipping out of first in the NHL.

items.text: Lucas Raymond extended his point streak against Ottawa to eight games.

The Senators were without Artem Zub, Jake Sanderson and André Burakovsky. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Ducks and the Islanders were missing more at the time.
Two of the preview’s four calls held.
